`stock_report.py` now flags an item as `REORDER` when what's on hand is at or below what you'd expect to sell in the 6 days an order takes to arrive. `LEAD_TIME_DAYS = 6` sits at the top of the file, just under the imports.

I ran it against your current `inventory.csv`:

```
SKU      ITEM                       ON HAND  STATUS
CF-1K    House blend 1kg                  9  REORDER
CF-250   Colombia beans 250g             42  ok
FL-100   Paper filters x100               0  OUT
MG-12    Enamel mug                      18  ok
OT-1L    Oat milk 1L                     30  REORDER
TE-50    Breakfast tea x50               25  ok
```

House blend has 9 on hand against about 14 expected to sell in 6 days, and oat milk has 30 against 45, so both get flagged. An empty shelf still shows `OUT`.

- **Exact ties are flagged:** an item with exactly 6 days of stock shows `REORDER`, since it would run out the day the delivery lands.
- **No safety margin:** the flag fires at exactly 6 days of average sales, so a busier-than-average week can still empty the shelf before the boxes arrive. Setting the number to 7 or 8 would give you a buffer.
